        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 9f94751ab1334862c2b470e35eb1bf59af5347e7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bob Peterson <rpeterso@redhat.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2015 09:05:31 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] GFS2: Fix rgrp end rounding problem for bsize < page size

[ Upstream commit 31dddd9eb9ebae9a2a9b502750e9e481d752180a ]

This patch fixes a bug introduced by commit 7005c3e. That patch
tries to map a vm range for resource groups, but the calculation
breaks down when the block size is less than the page size.

Signed-off-by: Bob Peterson <rpeterso@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Lee Jones <lee.jones@linaro.org>
Change-Id: I33423a43e33a2c7d162322281dfa3a70d2769900
---
 fs/gfs2/rgrp.c | 5 +++--
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/gfs2/rgrp.c b/fs/gfs2/rgrp.c
index 7474c413ffd1..a27201fbe1c6 100644
--- a/fs/gfs2/rgrp.c
+++ b/fs/gfs2/rgrp.c
@@ -933,8 +933,9 @@ static int read_rindex_entry(struct gfs2_inode *ip)
 		goto fail;
 
 	rgd->rd_gl->gl_object = rgd;
-	rgd->rd_gl->gl_vm.start = rgd->rd_addr * bsize;
-	rgd->rd_gl->gl_vm.end = rgd->rd_gl->gl_vm.start + (rgd->rd_length * bsize) - 1;
+	rgd->rd_gl->gl_vm.start = (rgd->rd_addr * bsize) & PAGE_CACHE_MASK;
+	rgd->rd_gl->gl_vm.end = PAGE_CACHE_ALIGN((rgd->rd_addr +
+						  rgd->rd_length) * bsize) - 1;
 	rgd->rd_rgl = (struct gfs2_rgrp_lvb *)rgd->rd_gl->gl_lksb.sb_lvbptr;
 	rgd->rd_flags &= ~GFS2_RDF_UPTODATE;
 	if (rgd->rd_data > sdp->sd_max_rg_data)
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by incorrect calculations for the virtual memory range of resource groups when the block size (bsize) is less than the page size. The original code did not account for the alignment requirements, leading to potential misalignment of memory addresses and incorrect mapping of resource groups. This was introduced by a previous commit that attempted to map the virtual memory range without considering the relationship between block size and page size. The patch corrects this by using PAGE_CACHE_MASK and PAGE_CACHE_ALIGN to ensure proper alignment and rounding of the memory addresses.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by incorrect calculations for the virtual memory range of resource groups when the block size (bsize) is less than the page size. The original code did not account for the alignment requirements, leading to potential misalignment of memory addresses and incorrect mapping of resource groups. This was introduced by a previous commit that attempted to map the virtual memory range without considering the relationship between block size and page size. The patch corrects this by using PAGE_CACHE_MASK and PAGE_CACHE_ALIGN to ensure proper alignment and rounding of the memory addresses.
